artifacts.title: Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Acree attempted to file a BCO 43-1 complaint with Presbytery against an action taken at a Presbytery meeting he did not attend as a commissioner. The SJC found the case administratively out of order because Acree lacked standing, not having been a commissioner at the meeting where the action was taken.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE Evans under BCO 38-1 without properly securing his approval of the full statement of facts, as the Investigative Committee's report added additional adverse facts he had not seen or approved. The SJC sustained the complaints of Evans and Pitts et al., annulled the deposition, and remanded the matter to AZP for action consistent with BCO 38-1 requirements; a lengthy concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively analyzed BCO 38-1 confession procedures.

artifacts.title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

artifacts.title: Aven v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Following the SJC's 2014-01 remand directing Ohio Valley Presbytery to 'hear further' from TE Hickey regarding his stated difference on Larger Catechism 177 (paedocommunion), the SJC denied Aven's complaint that OVP failed adequately to comply, finding that OVP did sufficiently hear further from the minister. A significant dissent argued OVP did not satisfy the specific directives from Case 2014-01.

The SJC found that Presbyterian judicial procedures were not followed as required by BCO 32, particularly regarding proper service of indictment and notice. The case was therefore remanded to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with BCO 32.

artifacts.synopsis: Antioch Session complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery erred in licensing Arthur Peterson given his divorce/remarriage history and his views on creation and a local flood. The SJC did not sustain the complaint on Issue 1 (licensure approval, 13-4), finding ECP acted with constitutional thoroughness and that precedent permitted a divorced man to hold office under certain conditions, but did sustain Issue 2 (3-0 panel; 17-0 SJC), finding ECP negligent in allowing Peterson to serve as stated supply for over six months before licensing him.

artifacts.title: Hopper v. James River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Robert D. Hopper, pastor of Grace Covenant Church in Williamsburg, Virginia, challenged James River Presbytery's April 1991 action forbidding him from preaching and teaching views affirming that the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit (including prophecy and tongues) may be present in the church in the present age. The Standing Judicial Commission denied the complaint, holding that presbytery has constitutional authority under BCO 13-9 and 34-5 to restrict teaching and preaching when it determines such views may be harmful to the spiritual welfare of the churches under its care, and that such restriction does not violate liberty of conscience absent a determination that the forbidden teaching is heretical.
